title: Observability tabletop exercises, fallbacks & rollout checklist
content:
Purpose:
Run focused, small-group tabletop exercises that validate observability coverage for common rollout and fallback scenarios. This doc is a lightweight facilitator guide + checklist for 60–90 minute sessions. Use this to: discover telemetry gaps, validate dashboards & traces, confirm escalation paths, and exercise graceful degradation paths.

Audience:
- Primary: SRE/observability, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api engineers
- Secondary: solutions-eng, oncall, product managers for major rollouts

When to run:
- Before any model family rollout that changes batching/cache behavior (canary start)
- Before capacity or region rollouts for Dedicated/Private customers
- Quarterly as part of oncall readiness drills
- After major telemetry changes (sampling, tag changes, new signals)

Roles/players (sample):
- Facilitator (obs eng) — runs the exercise, keeps time
- Scribe — records decisions, gaps, action items in a ticket
- Oncall rep — executes quick mitigations and reads runbooks
- Platform/infra rep — validates capacity/failover knobs
- Product owner — observes impact to SLAs and business constraints

Pre-reqs (15–30m prep):
- Wire up a small synthetic traffic generator or use saved replay to simulate load patterns
- Ensure dashboards openable via shared link (Latency heatmap, Per-model SLI, Token/sec, KV cache hit ratio, Batching size distribution, Error rate by tenant)
- Enable debug tracing for the session or increase sampling for a short window (note sampling changes)
- Create ephemeral Slack channel: #tt-obs-<date>-<scenario>

Scenarios (pick 1–2 per session):
1) Canary rollout regression: new quantized model variant is rolled to 10% traffic and latency regresses for long-context requests.
   - Trigger: synthetic long-context traffic spike.
   - Observe: p95/p99 per-model latency, backend worker queue length, KV cache miss rate, model fallback count, error budget burn.
   - Trace anchors: request root span, model selection span, kernel-compile/quantize span, cache-lookup span.
   - Expected operator actions: pause canary, fail traffic to previous stable model, open postmortem ticket.

2) KV-cache cold start for multi-tenant burst: cold-cache leads to high tokens/sec and increased p95.
   - Trigger: tenant replay with cold prefixes.
   - Observe: cache-warmup rate, per-tenant cost spike, CPU/GPU utilization, async pre-warm tasks.
   - Check fallback: are cached-prefix fast-path metrics attached to spans? If missing, note instrumentation gap.

3) Routing/region outage with automatic fallback: region A fails and routing should send traffic to region B with compatible model variants.
   - Trigger: simulated region loss (failover).
   - Observe: routing decision logs, fallback policy traces, cross-region latency delta, fallback model variant quality tag.
   - Escalation: if fallback triggers model downgrade, product PM notified.

4) Dedicated capacity saturation: throttles applied and queued requests are dropped or retried.
   - Trigger: synthetic sustained throughput > reserved capacity.
   - Observe: throttle rate, retry bursts, tenant error surface, SLA breach alarms.
   - Runbook: scale burst capacity or enable soft-fallback to hosted API; validate that alerts are actionable.

Facilitator checklist (session flow):
- [ ] Announce scenario and goals (5m)
- [ ] Verify dashboards and tracing window (5m)
- [ ] Execute trigger/synthetic traffic (10–20m)
- [ ] Observe metrics and traces live (15–25m)
- [ ] Run remediation steps (10–15m)
- [ ] Capture action items and assign owners (5m)
- [ ] Quick retrospective and follow-up ticket creation (5m)

Dashboards & queries to open (minimum):
- Latency heatmap (per-model, per-tenant) with p50/p95/p99 lines
- Token/sec and tokens-per-request time series with cost overlay
- KV cache hit/miss ratio with warmup trend and per-tenant breakdown
- Batch size distribution histogram and queue length per-worker
- Model-fallback events timeline (annotated with rollouts and routing decisions)
- Error rate by error class and tenant (with sample trace links)
- Alerting panel: active SLO burn, oncall page history, escalation status

Tracing anchors & what to look for:
- Root span: request incoming -> confirm tenant id, route decision metadata, request size annotations
- Cache lookup span: low latency + miss flag vs high latency on miss; ensure tenant tag present
- Model selection span: variant id, quantization profile, kernel selection hint
- Inference span(s): token-production rate, blocking waits, GPU kernel time vs CPU overhead
- Fallback path spans: clear markers showing fallback decision + reason (e.g., latency_sla_exceeded / capacity_full)
- Sampling note: if we increased sampling for the exercise, annotate traces so they are excluded from production metrics backfills

Common instrumentation gaps to watch for (notes-to-self):
- Missing tenant tag on inner spans (makes multi-tenant troubleshooting painful)
- No explicit span for "routing decision" -> harder to audit fallbacks
- Cache warmup is visible as fill-rate but not correlated to p95 regressions in dashboards
- Batching size distribution not collected per worker type

Escalation criteria (fast checks):
- p95 latency > SLO for > 5 minutes AND error rate increase > 0.5% -> escalate to SRE pager
- Cost per token doubles for a single tenant in 10m window -> alert billing-signal and solutions-eng
- Model fallback rate > 2% of requests for 15m -> product and model-ops review

Post-exercise outputs (required):
- Create ticket: OBS-TT-<date>-<scenario> with summary, gaps, and owners
- If telemetry gaps found, include concrete instrumentation PR suggestions (span name, tags, metric name)
- Schedule follow-up to verify fixes (target: 2 weeks)
- Update dashboard links in central "obs-dashboard-inventory" doc if changed

Template Slack snippet (post session):
"Tabletop exercise (canary regression) completed. Summary: observed p95 increase due to cold-cache; key gaps: missing routing span, no per-worker batching histogram. Actions: OBS-1234 (add routing span) owner: @riley; OBS-1235 (batch histogram) owner: @samir. Follow-up in 2 weeks. Logs + traces: <link>."

Reminders & heuristics:
- Keep sessions small and timeboxed: 60m max. Two scenarios are ambitious for one session.
- Prioritize telemetry changes that unblock fast triage (tenant tags, routing spans, cache flags).
- When changing sampling for an exercise, document the window and exclude from long-term SLIs/backfill jobs.

Appendix: quick instrumentation naming suggestions (examples to copy-paste into PRs)
- spans: "request.inbound", "route.decision", "cache.lookup", "model.select", "inference.generate"
- metrics: "inference.latency_ms.p95", "kv_cache.hit_ratio", "batch.size.histogram", "fallback.count"

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Try a "postmortem lite" for exercises where remediation was non-trivial. Keep it short: what happened, gaps, fix ETA.
- Capture a sample trace id and attach to ticket for devs to reproduce the breadcrumb.

End of doc.
